coreOverlap: Core overlap and incremental diagnostic benefit remain unmeasured.
assessment: Manual semantic assessment; offline tests check the finite authored job, not model reasoning.
protectedReasoning: The standalone offline job has five records and two workers; no request-serving deadline or shared request pool is required by its contract.
Every operation settles after a finite logical interval and releases its slot on success or failure. At most two operations/timers are active; all five finish after three rounds.
An item failure is recorded without retry and the remaining records finish; the observed long duration alone establishes no timeout/cancellation defect.
Protection is limited to this supplied finite job, not a blanket claim that all batch jobs are safe or never need deadlines.
forbiddenClaims: Long duration or absence of a request timer proves a timeout defect despite the finite offline contract.
An interactive request SLO, external traffic contention, unbounded dependency or cancellation requirement exists.
The job must add a request timeout, circuit breaker or process split without a supported diagnosis.
A selected item failure means capacity is leaked or remaining records never finish.
This fixture proves universal production safety, real wall-clock duration, model quality or measured incremental benefit.
